candidates.title: Emotional Seniority
candidates.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who understands this relationship best, and treat your interpretation as the one that should settle disagreements.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Relationship Knots stance for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Keeper of the Peace
candidates.instruction: Project calm authority over the relationship while carefully avoiding anything that might expose how fragile the peace really is.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Relationship Knots stance for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: I Know Your Tells
candidates.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

candidates.title: Still Part of This
candidates.instruction: Act as though shared history permanently guarantees your place, even when present boundaries suggest otherwise.

candidates.title: Keeper of Precedent
candidates.instruction: Treat your longer memory as an archive, not a throne. Cite specific promises and precedents whenever the relationship faces a new choice.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Relationship Knots stance for this required subtheme slot.

editorialRevision.reason: Uses specific precedent as guidance instead of claiming superior authority to interpret the entire relationship.

candidates.title: Private Access

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Relationship Knots stance for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Our Private Language

candidates.title: I Was There

candidates.title: Back in Our Roles

candidates.title: The Other Favorite

candidates.title: Old Reflex

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Relationship Knots stance for this required subtheme slot.

editorialRevision.reason: Centers involuntary relationship habit rather than exclusive trust and concealed dependence.

candidates.title: Here We Go Again
candidates.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Relationship Knots engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.title: The Family Historian
candidates.instruction: Treat your memory of shared events as the official version and correct details that weaken the connection.
candidates.rationale: Strong memory-keeper behavior, but Our Private Language creates more immediate interaction and less factual correction.

candidates.title: Favorite by Tradition
candidates.instruction: Act as though old affection grants permanent priority, even when the present relationship has changed.
candidates.rationale: Playable entitlement, but it overlaps Still Part of This and may narrow scenes toward family or romantic favoritism.

candidates.title: Protective Distance
candidates.instruction: Treat withdrawal as the kindest way to protect the relationship, and resist every attempt to make closeness immediate.
candidates.rationale: Promising emotional contradiction, but it fits the later Emotional Pressure pack more naturally than this broad relationship pack.

candidates.title: Every Goodbye Is Temporary
candidates.instruction: Interpret every departure as a dramatic pause in a connection that cannot truly end.
candidates.rationale: Clear and playable, but it overlaps both A Sign We’re Fine and Fate Keeps Reconnecting Us within the selected set.

candidates.title: Your Best Friend Is Jealous
candidates.instruction: Your partner is jealous of every other relationship you have and will compete for attention.
candidates.rationale: Violates the hidden-information rule by declaring another performer’s private emotion and future behavior.

candidates.title: Divorced at Dinner
candidates.instruction: Behave like former spouses forced to share one tense meal.
candidates.rationale: Predefines a specific relationship and setting instead of supplying a portable holder-specific stance.

candidates.title: Be Toxic
candidates.instruction: Be manipulative, possessive, and emotionally unhealthy.
candidates.rationale: Vague, stigmatizing, and lacking an observable repeatable behavior or escalation path.

candidates.title: Secretly in Love
candidates.instruction: Hide that you are secretly in love with the other performer.
candidates.rationale: Primarily an internal fact and familiar cliché; it does not tell the holder how to behave responsively.

candidates.title: Say It First
candidates.instruction: Get someone to name the feeling between you before you reveal your own.
candidates.rationale: Subtle and useful, but Say You Missed Me supplies more concrete playable targets for the first playtest set.

candidates.title: Use the Old Nickname
candidates.instruction: Get someone to use a familiar name or phrase that confirms the old connection still exists.
candidates.rationale: A memorable action, but it depends on inventing a specific token and is less portable than Acknowledge Our History.

candidates.title: One More Memory
candidates.instruction: Keep someone present by opening one more shared memory whenever the conversation seems finished.
candidates.rationale: Strong nostalgic retention behavior, but Stay Until We’re Okay creates a broader repair engine.

candidates.title: Introduce Me Properly
candidates.instruction: Get someone to describe your relationship in a way that confirms your importance.
candidates.rationale: Potentially useful for public-status scenes, but it can push the partner toward explanatory exposition.

candidates.title: Force a Hug
candidates.instruction: Make someone accept physical affection before the scene can continue.
candidates.rationale: Requires coerced physical contact and violates the game’s safety and consent standards.

candidates.title: Break Them Up
candidates.instruction: Convince someone to end an offstage relationship so you can have them back.
candidates.rationale: Overly specific, manipulative, and dependent on an absent third party rather than the present interaction.

candidates.title: Make Them Love You
candidates.instruction: Make someone fall in love with you before the scene ends.
candidates.rationale: Attempts to guarantee another performer’s private emotional state and supplies no realistic playable route.

candidates.title: Win the Breakup
candidates.instruction: Turn the end of a romantic relationship into a contest over who is happier.
candidates.rationale: Playable but unnecessarily relationship- and situation-specific; its contest engine fits Competition & Consequences better.
